transcript.text: Section 1.
You will hear a man talking first to a receptionist and then to a doctor at a health centre.
First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 3 on page 2.
You will see that there is an example that has been done for you.
On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
Receptionist: Good morning, how can I help you?
Patient: Yes, I am a visitor to this area.
I had a sporting accident a little while ago and I am still in some pain and I wondered
if I could see a doctor here.
Receptionist: Certainly sir, we can take you on as a temporary patient.
I will just take down some personal details.
Can I start with your name?
Patient: Yes, it is Peter.
Peter Smith. Peter Smith。
The patient's name is Peter Smith.
So Peter Smith has been written in the space.
Now we shall begin.
You should answer the questions as you listen because you will not hear the recording
a second time.
Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 3.
Receptionist: Good morning, how can I help you?
Patient: Yes, I am a visitor to this area.
I had a sporting accident a little while ago and I am still in some pain and I wondered
if I could see a doctor here.
Receptionist: Certainly sir, we can take you on as a temporary patient.
I will just take down some personal details.
Can I start with your name?
Patient: Yes, it is Peter.
Peter Smith. Peter Smith。
Receptionist: Right, Peter.
And where are you staying here?
Patient: At 95 Cross Street.
Receptionist: And the suburb?
Patient: Walkley, that is W-A-L-K-L-E-Y.
Receptionist: And can I have a contact phone number?
Patient: It is 4689-5324.
Receptionist: Thanks.
Okay.
If you just wait down there, the doctor will see you in a minute.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 4
to 10 on page 2.
Now listen and answer questions 4 to 10.
Doctor: Now what can I do for you?
It is Peter Smith, isn't it?
Patient: Yes, I had a sporting accident and was treated by a doctor at home but I am still in pain.
Doctor: Right, I just need to ask you a few questions first of all.
Patient: Fine.
Doctor: Now, what sport were you doing?
Patient: I was playing tennis.
Doctor: Oh, I see.
And what was the nature of your injury?
Did you hurt your elbow or wrist?
Patient: No, I had a sprained knee.
That was the original problem.
Doctor: Right.
And when did this happen?
Patient: It was three weeks ago now.
So that was June 18th.
Doctor: Fine.
And you say you had medical treatment?
Patient: Yes.
The doctor said I didn't need an x-ray or anything and he just told me to use an ice pack.
Doctor: Fine.
Patient: Yes, and I've been using a walking stick to help me get around.
Doctor: Right.
Now, what problems are you experiencing at the moment?
Are you having any problems walking?
Patient: Well, I can walk okay but I still can't go upstairs so I've been sleeping downstairs.
Doctor: Hmm.
Now, you say your knee still hurts?
Patient: Well, no.
Actually, it's recovering nicely.
It's my back that's hurting me now.
It really aches at night and I can hardly sleep.
Doctor: Well, there's a few different things I can suggest for that.
Patient: Great.
Doctor: First, you should put your stick away as that's probably the source of the problem.
It'll be making you unbalanced.
Patient: Oh, really?
I wish I'd known.
Doctor: After that, I can prescribe you something to relax the muscles in your back.
Patient: Oh, sorry to be difficult but I've had something like that in the past and there were
lots of side effects and I had to stop taking it.
Can you recommend anything else?
Doctor: Well, yes, we do have a leaflet showing some exercises you can do to help yourself at
home.
If you do them every day, they'll soon be effective.
Patient: Great.
I'll do that.
That is the end of section one.
You now have half a minute to check your answers.
All right.
Thank you.
